license_eligibility_enforcement: Before substantive acquisition, create a pinned path allowlist using repository metadata and small license/header inspections only. Resolve each file against its nearest applicable LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE, explicit SPDX/header, third-party provenance and repository inheritance; absence of a header alone is not proof of missing rights or proof of eligibility.

Each accepted file records source commit, path/blob identity, license identifier/version, license-text SHA-256, controlling notice paths and hashes, copyright/attribution, inherited-scope rationale, modification obligations and eligibility decision. Payload SHA-256 is added and verified on authorized retrieval.

Allow only reviewed PSF-2.0/historical CPython terms, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 and applicable 0BSD examples for these proposed code subsets. Any additional license requires explicit review, not automatic inheritance from the root license. Unlicensed, conflicting, noncommercial, no-derivatives, custom/unknown and unresolved mixed content is REJECT for this pilot.

Default-exclude third-party/vendor/submodule trees and copied examples unless separately reviewed. License detectors may flag candidates but cannot grant eligibility; unexpected headers on acquisition quarantine the file and stop its source for review.

Do not flatten the combined corpus under one aggregate permissive license. Retain per-document notices and full source provenance; preserve attribution and change notices when redistributing source/cleaned extracts. Exclude uncertain passages instead of removing their notices.
All inputs remain inert: no downloaded-code imports, builds, installation hooks, tests or proof execution. Secret/PII scans reject suspect documents; logs store hashes/reasons without secret values.
